988:   Label slow_path;
989:   if (JvmtiExport::can_post_interpreter_events()) {
990:     __ ldrw(rscratch1, Address(rthread, JavaThread::interp_only_mode_offset()));
991:     __ cbnzw(rscratch1, slow_path);
992:   }
993:   __ safepoint_poll(slow_path, false /* at_return */, false /* in_nmethod */);
994: #if INCLUDE_JVMTI
995:   // Breakpoint events alone do not put the thread in interpreter-only mode.
996:   Label no_breakpoints;
997:   __ ldr(rscratch1, Address(rmethod, Method::method_counters_offset()));
998:   __ cbz(rscratch1, no_breakpoints);
999:   __ ldrh(rscratch1, Address(rscratch1, in_bytes(MethodCounters::number_of_breakpoints_offset())));
1000:   __ cbnzw(rscratch1, slow_path);
1001:   __ bind(no_breakpoints);
1002: #endif
1003:   if (CommonIntrinsics::is_scalar(id)) {
1004:     bool binary = CommonIntrinsics::is_binary_scalar(id);
1005:     bool wide = CommonIntrinsics::scalar_is_wide(id);
1006:     int offset = binary ? (wide ? 2 : 1) * wordSize : 0;
1007:     __ ldr(r0, Address(esp, offset));
1008:     if (binary) __ ldr(r1, Address(esp, 0));
1009:     common_scalar_intrinsic(_masm, id, r0, r0, binary ? r1 : noreg, r2, r3, v0, &slow_path);
1010:     __ andr(sp, r19_sender_sp, -16);
1011:     __ ret(lr);
1012:     __ bind(slow_path);
1013:     __ jump_to_entry(Interpreter::entry_for_kind(Interpreter::zerolocals));
1014:     return entry;
1015:   }
1016:   if (CommonIntrinsics::needs_compiler_stubs(id)) {
1017:     __ lea(rscratch1, ExternalAddress(StubRoutines::compiler_stubs_initialized_address()));
1018:     __ ldarb(rscratch2, rscratch1);
1019:     __ cbz(rscratch2, slow_path);
1020:   }
1021:   // Arguments stay on the expression stack so the Java fallback can reuse them.
1022:   __ mov(c_rarg0, esp);
1023:   __ stp(rscratch2, lr, Address(__ pre(sp, -2 * wordSize)));
1024:   __ super_call_VM_leaf(CommonIntrinsics::entry_for(id), c_rarg0);
1025:   __ ldp(rscratch2, lr, Address(__ post(sp, 2 * wordSize)));
1026:   __ mov(rscratch1, CommonIntrinsics::fallback);
1027:   __ cmp(r0, rscratch1);
1028:   __ br(Assembler::EQ, slow_path);
1029:   __ andr(sp, r19_sender_sp, -16);
1030:   __ ret(lr);
1031:   __ bind(slow_path);
1032:   __ jump_to_entry(Interpreter::entry_for_kind(Interpreter::zerolocals));

src/hotspot/share/interpreter/abstractInterpreter.hpp
141:   static MethodKind method_kind(const methodHandle& m);
142:   static address    entry_for_kind(MethodKind k)                { assert(0 <= k && k < number_of_method_entries, "illegal kind"); return _entry_table[k]; }
143:   static address    entry_for_method(const methodHandle& m) {
144:     vmIntrinsics::ID id = m->intrinsic_id();
145:     if (id != vmIntrinsics::_none) {
146:       address common_entry = _common_entry_table[vmIntrinsics::as_int(id)];
147:       if (common_entry != nullptr && !m->is_synchronized() && !m->is_native()) {
148:         return common_entry;
149:       }
150:     }
151:     return entry_for_kind(method_kind(m));
152:   }

249:   // Keep the ordinary bytecode layout independent of optional intrinsic
250:   // entries. Changes to intrinsic flags or alias sharing must not reposition
251:   // hot Java fallback handlers. Deoptimization entries remain last.
252: #if defined(AMD64) || defined(AARCH64)
253:   // A safepoint can select the Java fallback of an intrinsic entry. During a
254:   // static archive assembly that would make archived constant-pool resolution
255:   // depend on safepoint timing. AOT training clears those entries in its
256:   // preimage and can retain the common entries while running the application.
257:   if (CommonIntrinsics::enabled() && InlineIntrinsics &&
258:       (!CDSConfig::is_dumping_static_archive() || CDSConfig::is_dumping_preimage_static_archive())) {
259:     TraceTime timer("Common intrinsic entry generation", TRACETIME_LOG(Debug, startuptime));
260:     CodeletMark cm(_masm, "common intrinsic entry points");
261:     // Visit only our catalogue. Most VM intrinsics have no common entry.
262: #define COMMON_ID(id, slots, result) vmIntrinsics::id,
263:     static const vmIntrinsics::ID ids[] = {
264:       COMMON_INTRINSICS_DO(COMMON_ID)
265:       COMMON_SCALAR_INTRINSICS_DO(COMMON_ID)
266:       COMMON_BINARY_SCALAR_INTRINSICS_DO(COMMON_ID)
267:       vmIntrinsics::_vectorizedHashCodeLeaf
268:     };
269: #undef COMMON_ID
270:     for (vmIntrinsics::ID id : ids) {
271:       if (CommonIntrinsics::is_available_for_interpreter(id) && vmIntrinsics::is_intrinsic_available(id)) {
272:         // These aliases have identical arguments, operations and guards.
273:         // Check each ID's flags above even when its code can be shared.
274:         vmIntrinsics::ID canonical = id;
275:         switch (id) {
276:           case vmIntrinsics::_min_strict: canonical = vmIntrinsics::_min; break;
277:           case vmIntrinsics::_max_strict: canonical = vmIntrinsics::_max; break;
278:           case vmIntrinsics::_vectorizedHashCodeLeaf: canonical = vmIntrinsics::_vectorizedHashCode; break;
279:           default: break;
280:         }
281:         address entry = Interpreter::_common_entry_table[vmIntrinsics::as_int(canonical)];
282:         if (entry == nullptr) {
283:           __ align(CodeEntryAlignment);
284:           entry = generate_common_intrinsic_entry(id);
285:         }
286:         Interpreter::_common_entry_table[vmIntrinsics::as_int(id)] = entry;
287:       }
288:     }
289:   }
290: #endif

835: void InterpreterRuntime::update_invoke_cp_cache_entry(CallInfo& info, Bytecodes::Code bytecode,
836:                                                       methodHandle& resolved_method,
837:                                                       constantPoolHandle& pool,
838:                                                       int method_index, bool cache_call) {
839:   // Don't allow safepoints until the method is cached.
840:   NoSafepointVerifier nsv;

842:   // Common-intrinsic preparation may have blocked after resolution. CallInfo
843:   // keeps the old method alive and follows redefinition to the current version.
844:   // Refresh under this verifier so publication cannot cache an obsolete method.
845:   resolved_method = methodHandle(Thread::current(), info.resolved_method());

851: #ifdef ASSERT
852:   if (bytecode == Bytecodes::_invokeinterface) {
853:     if (resolved_method->method_holder() == vmClasses::Object_klass()) {
854:       // NOTE: THIS IS A FIX FOR A CORNER CASE in the JVM spec

860:     } else if (!resolved_method->has_itable_index()) {
861:       // Resolved something like CharSequence.toString.  Use vtable not itable.

867:       assert(info.itable_index() == index, "");
868:     }
869:   } else if (bytecode == Bytecodes::_invokespecial) {
870:     assert(info.call_kind() == CallInfo::direct_call, "must be direct call");
871:   } else {
872:     assert(info.call_kind() == CallInfo::direct_call ||
873:            info.call_kind() == CallInfo::vtable_call, "");
874:   }
875: #endif

src/hotspot/share/oops/cpCache.cpp
557: bool ConstantPoolCache::can_archive_resolved_method(ConstantPool* src_cp, ResolvedMethodEntry* method_entry, const char*& rejection_reason) {
558:   InstanceKlass* pool_holder = constant_pool()->pool_holder();
559:   if (pool_holder->defined_by_other_loaders()) {
560:     // Archiving resolved cp entries for classes from non-builtin loaders
561:     // is not yet supported.
562:     rejection_reason = "(pool holder comes from a non-builtin loader)";
563:     return false;
564:   }
565: 
566:   if (CDSConfig::is_dumping_dynamic_archive()) {
567:     // InstanceKlass::methods() has been resorted. We need to
568:     // update the vtable_index in method_entry (not implemented)
569:     rejection_reason = "(InstanceKlass::methods() has been resorted)";
570:     return false;
571:   }
572: 
573:   int cp_index = method_entry->constant_pool_index();
574: 
575:   if (!method_entry->is_resolved(Bytecodes::_invokevirtual)) {
576:     if (method_entry->method() == nullptr) {
577:       rejection_reason = "(method entry is not resolved)";
578:       return false;
579:     }
580:     if (method_entry->method()->is_continuation_native_intrinsic()) {
581:       rejection_reason = "(corresponding stub is generated on demand during method resolution)";
582:       return false; // FIXME: corresponding stub is generated on demand during method resolution (see LinkResolver::resolve_static_call).
583:     }
584:     if (method_entry->is_resolved(Bytecodes::_invokehandle)) {
585:       if (!CDSConfig::is_dumping_method_handles()) {
586:         rejection_reason = "(not dumping method handles)";
587:         return false;
588:       }
589: 
590:       Symbol* sig = constant_pool()->uncached_signature_ref_at(cp_index);
591:       Klass* k;
592:       if (!AOTConstantPoolResolver::check_methodtype_signature(constant_pool(), sig, &k, true)) {
593:         // invokehandles that were resolved in the training run should have been filtered in
594:         // AOTConstantPoolResolver::maybe_resolve_fmi_ref so we shouldn't come to here.
595:         //
596:         // If we come here it's because the AOT assembly phase has executed an invokehandle
597:         // that uses an excluded type like jdk.jfr.Event. This should not happen because the
598:         // AOT assembly phase should execute only a very limited set of Java code.
599:         ResourceMark rm;
600:         fatal("AOT assembly phase must not resolve any invokehandles whose signatures include an excluded type");
601:       }
602:     }
603:     if (method_entry->method()->is_method_handle_intrinsic() && !CDSConfig::is_dumping_method_handles()) {
604:       rejection_reason = "(not dumping intrinsic method handles)";
605:       return false;
606:     }
607:   }
608: 
609:   assert(src_cp->tag_at(cp_index).is_method() || src_cp->tag_at(cp_index).is_interface_method(), "sanity");
610: 
611:   if (!AOTConstantPoolResolver::is_resolution_deterministic(src_cp, cp_index)) {
612:       rejection_reason = "(resolution is not deterministic)";
613:     return false;
614:   }
615:   return true;
616: }

src/hotspot/share/oops/constantPool.cpp
537: void ConstantPool::remove_resolved_klass_if_non_deterministic(int cp_index) {
538:   assert(ArchiveBuilder::current()->is_in_buffer_space(this), "must be");
539:   assert(tag_at(cp_index).is_klass(), "must be resolved");
540: 
541:   bool can_archive;
542:   Klass* k = nullptr;
543: 
544:   if (CDSConfig::is_dumping_preimage_static_archive()) {
545:     can_archive = false;
546:   } else {
547:     k = resolved_klass_at(cp_index);
548:     if (k == nullptr) {
549:       // We'd come here if the referenced class has been excluded via
550:       // SystemDictionaryShared::is_excluded_class(). As a result, ArchiveBuilder
551:       // has cleared the resolved_klasses()->at(...) pointer to null. Thus, we
552:       // need to revert the tag to JVM_CONSTANT_UnresolvedClass.
553:       can_archive = false;
554:     } else {
555:       ConstantPool* src_cp = ArchiveBuilder::current()->get_source_addr(this);
556:       can_archive = AOTConstantPoolResolver::is_resolution_deterministic(src_cp, cp_index);
557:     }
558:   }
559: 
560:   if (!can_archive) {
561:     int resolved_klass_index = klass_slot_at(cp_index).resolved_klass_index();
562:     // This might be at a safepoint but do this in the right order.
563:     tag_at_put(cp_index, JVM_CONSTANT_UnresolvedClass);
564:     resolved_klasses()->at_put(resolved_klass_index, nullptr);
565:   }

src/hotspot/share/cds/aotConstantPoolResolver.cpp
40: // Returns true if we CAN PROVE that cp_index will always resolve to
41: // the same information at both dump time and run time. This is a
42: // necessary (but not sufficient) condition for pre-resolving cp_index
43: // during CDS archive assembly.
44: bool AOTConstantPoolResolver::is_resolution_deterministic(ConstantPool* cp, int cp_index) {
45:   assert(!is_in_archivebuilder_buffer(cp), "sanity");
46: 
47:   if (cp->tag_at(cp_index).is_klass()) {
48:     // We require cp_index to be already resolved. This is fine for now, are we
49:     // currently archive only CP entries that are already resolved.
50:     Klass* resolved_klass = cp->resolved_klass_at(cp_index);
51:     return resolved_klass != nullptr && is_class_resolution_deterministic(cp->pool_holder(), resolved_klass);
52:   } else if (cp->tag_at(cp_index).is_invoke_dynamic()) {
53:     return is_indy_resolution_deterministic(cp, cp_index);
54:   } else if (cp->tag_at(cp_index).is_field() ||
55:              cp->tag_at(cp_index).is_method() ||
56:              cp->tag_at(cp_index).is_interface_method()) {
57:     int klass_cp_index = cp->uncached_klass_ref_index_at(cp_index);
58:     if (!cp->tag_at(klass_cp_index).is_klass()) {
59:       // Not yet resolved
60:       return false;
61:     }
62:     Klass* k = cp->resolved_klass_at(klass_cp_index);
63:     if (!is_class_resolution_deterministic(cp->pool_holder(), k)) {
64:       return false;
65:     }
66: 
67:     if (!k->is_instance_klass()) {
68:       // TODO: support non instance klasses as well.
69:       return false;
70:     }
71: 
72:     // Here, We don't check if this entry can actually be resolved to a valid Field/Method.
73:     // This method should be called by the ConstantPool to check Fields/Methods that
74:     // have already been successfully resolved.
75:     return true;
76:   } else {

669:         // for methods collected during training run, then waits for all compilations

672:         // with AOT and -Xcomp.
673:         Arguments::set_mode_flags(Arguments::_mixed);
674:       }
675:     } else if (!mode_flag_cmd_line) {
676:       // By default, -Xshare:dump runs in interpreter-only mode, which is required for deterministic archive.
677:       //
678:       // If your classlist is large and you don't care about deterministic dumping, you can use
679:       // -Xshare:dump -Xmixed to improve dumping speed.
680:       Arguments::set_mode_flags(Arguments::_int);
681:     } else if (Arguments::mode() == Arguments::_comp) {
682:       // -Xcomp may use excessive CPU for the test tiers. Also, -Xshare:dump runs a small and fixed set of
683:       // Java code, so there's not much benefit in running -Xcomp.

test/hotspot/jtreg/runtime/cds/DeterministicDump.java
66:     public static void doTest(boolean compressed, String... extraArgs) throws Exception {
67:         ArrayList<String> baseArgs = new ArrayList<>();
68:         baseArgs.addAll(Arrays.asList(extraArgs));
69: 
70:         // Try to reduce indeterminism of GC heap sizing and evacuation.
71:         baseArgs.add("-Xmx128M");
72:         baseArgs.add("-Xms128M");
73:         baseArgs.add("-Xmn120M");
74: 
75:         if (Platform.is64bit()) {
76:             // This option is available only on 64-bit.
77:             String sign = (compressed) ?  "+" : "-";
78:             baseArgs.add("-XX:" + sign + "UseCompressedOops");
79:         }
80: 
81:         String baseArchive = dump(baseArgs);
82:         File baseArchiveFile = new File(baseArchive + ".jsa");
83:         HEADER_SIZE = CDSArchiveUtils.fileHeaderSize(baseArchiveFile);
84: 
85:         // (1) Dump with the same args. Should produce the same archive.
86:         String baseArchive2 = dump(baseArgs);
87:         compare(baseArchive, baseArchive2, baseArchiveFile);
88: 
89:         // (2) This will cause the archive to be relocated during dump time. We should
90:         //     still get the same bits. This simulates relocation that happens when
91:         //     Address Space Layout Randomization prevents the archive space to
92:         //     be mapped at the default location.
93:         String relocatedArchive = dump(baseArgs, "-XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions", "-XX:ArchiveRelocationMode=1");
94:         compare(baseArchive, relocatedArchive, baseArchiveFile);
95:     }
96: 
97:     static int id = 0;
98:     static String dump(ArrayList<String> args, String... more) throws Exception {
99:         String logName = "SharedArchiveFile" + (id++);
100:         String archiveName = logName + ".jsa";
101:         String mapName = logName + ".map";
102:         CDSOptions opts = (new CDSOptions())
103:             .addPrefix("-Xint") // Override any -Xmixed/-Xcomp flags from jtreg -vmoptions
104:             .addPrefix("-Xlog:cds=debug,gc=debug")
105:             .addPrefix("-Xlog:aot+map*=trace:file=" + mapName + ":none:filesize=0")
106:             .setArchiveName(archiveName)
107:             .addSuffix(args)
108:             .addSuffix(more);
109:         CDSTestUtils.createArchiveAndCheck(opts);
110: 
111:         return logName;
112:     }
113: 
114:     static void compare(String file0, String file1, File archiveFile) throws Exception {
115:         byte[] buff0 = new byte[4096];
116:         byte[] buff1 = new byte[4096];
117:         try (FileInputStream in0 = new FileInputStream(file0 + ".jsa");
118:              FileInputStream in1 = new FileInputStream(file1 + ".jsa")) {
119:             int total = 0;
120:             while (true) {
121:                 int n0 = read(in0, buff0);
122:                 int n1 = read(in1, buff1);
123:                 if (n0 != n1) {
124:                     throw new RuntimeException("File contents (file sizes?) are different after " + total + " bytes; n0 = "
125:                                                + n0 + ", n1 = " + n1);
126:                 }
127:                 if (n0 == 0) {
128:                     System.out.println("File contents are the same: " + total + " bytes");
129:                     break;
130:                 }
131:                 for (int i = 0; i < n0; i++) {
132:                     byte b0 = buff0[i];
133:                     byte b1 = buff1[i];
134:                     if (b0 != b1) {
135:                         // The checksums are stored in the header so it should be skipped
136:                         // since we want to see the first meaningful diff between the archives
137:                         if (total + i > HEADER_SIZE) {
138:                             print_diff(file0 + ".map", file1 + ".map", archiveFile, total + i);
139:                             throw new RuntimeException("File content different at byte #" + (total + i) + ", b0 = " + b0 + ", b1 = " + b1);
140:                         }
141:                     }
142:                 }
143:                 total += n0;
144:             }
145:         }

test/lib/jdk/test/lib/cds/CDSTestUtils.java
245:     public static OutputAnalyzer createArchive(CDSOptions opts)
246:         throws Exception {
247: 
248:         startNewArchiveName();
249: 
250:         ArrayList<String> cmd = new ArrayList<String>();
251: 
252:         for (String p : opts.prefix) cmd.add(p);
253: 
254:         cmd.add("-Xshare:dump");
255:         cmd.add("-Xlog:cds,aot+hashtables");
256:         if (opts.archiveName == null)
257:             opts.archiveName = getDefaultArchiveName();
258:         cmd.add("-XX:SharedArchiveFile=" + opts.archiveName);
259: 
260:         if (opts.classList != null) {
261:             File classListFile = makeClassList(opts.classList);
262:             cmd.add("-XX:ExtraSharedClassListFile=" + classListFile.getPath());
263:         }
264: 
265:         for (String s : opts.suffix) cmd.add(s);
266: 
267:         String[] cmdLine = cmd.toArray(new String[cmd.size()]);
268:         ProcessBuilder pb = ProcessTools.createTestJavaProcessBuilder(cmdLine);
269:         return executeAndLog(pb, "dump");

test/lib/jdk/test/lib/process/ProcessTools.java
564:     public static ProcessBuilder createTestJavaProcessBuilder(String... command) {
565:         return createJavaProcessBuilder(Utils.prependTestJavaOpts(command));
566:     }

test/lib/jdk/test/lib/Utils.java
228:     public static String[] getTestJavaOpts() {
229:         List<String> opts = new ArrayList<String>();
230:         Collections.addAll(opts, safeSplitString(VM_OPTIONS));
231:         Collections.addAll(opts, safeSplitString(JAVA_OPTIONS));
232:         return opts.toArray(new String[0]);
233:     }
